headline: Yelp: a cash machine priced for terminal decline
subheadline: Advertising is shrinking, but AI products and data licensing are growing fast, and the stock trades at ~3x EBITDA
narrative: Yelp connects consumers with local businesses and earns most of its revenue from advertising by restaurants, retailers and service businesses.
Q3 2026 revenue fell 1% to $371m: advertising was down 6% as ad clicks fell 8%. Other revenue (Hatch, data licensing, food ordering) rose 82%.
Profitability is intact: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $92m (25% margin) and free cash flow $85m. Yelp bought back ~$200m of stock in 2026 to date.
At $20.34 the shares trade at about 3x EV/EBITDA, roughly 5x EBIT and 9x earnings, with net cash. That valuation implies a long, steep decline.
Even our structural-decline case (revenue –4% a year) is worth $25. A 50/50 blend with stabilisation gives a $33 target, but the debate is real.
market_pricing: The stock is down about 55% over three years, as AI answers threaten local-search traffic.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut for the second straight quarter, to $1.455–1.460bn.
Analysts are negative: 2 Buy, 6 Hold, 3 Sell or Strong Sell, with a median target of $22.

business.title: Local reviews and advertising, adding AI services and data licensing
business.subtitle: About 509,000 paying advertising locations, plus a fast-growing 'other revenue' line
overview: Headquartered in San Francisco and led by co-founder and CEO Jeremy Stoppelman.
Advertising is sold mainly to Services businesses (home and local services) and to Restaurants, Retail & Other (RR&O).
Yelp acquired Hatch (AI customer-communication software for service pros) in 2026: $264m of acquisition-related cash outflow year to date.

segments.name: Advertising (91% of Q3 revenue)
segments.text: Services $238m (–2%), RR&O $99m (–13%). Average cost per click +2%, ad clicks –8%.

segments.name: Other revenue (9%)
segments.text: $34m, up 82%: Hatch (~$37m annual run rate), data licensing with OpenAI and Meta, and food ordering. Target: $250m run rate by end-2028.

business.financials_title: Flat revenue, but margins doubled since 2022 and free cash flow is strong
financial_points: Revenue rose from $1.19bn (2022) to $1.47bn (2025). The EBIT margin improved from 5% to 13% as stock-based compensation fell.
2026 guidance: revenue $1.455–1.460bn and adjusted EBITDA $320–325m. SBC is ~7% of revenue and D&A ~5%.
Buybacks are paused to repay a $75m revolver drawing (used for Hatch). They are expected to resume in 2027.

industry.title: Local search is being rewired by AI
industry.subtitle: Fewer clicks reach publishers, but local data and reviews become more valuable to AI platforms
market: Local advertising follows small-business health. Yelp says restaurants, retail and home services are under pressure.
Industry studies suggest AI Overviews now appear in about 68% of local searches, which cuts click-throughs to sites like Yelp.
Yelp's content (reviews, photos, business data) is now licensed to AI companies, a new revenue stream.

tailwinds.title: Data licensing
tailwinds.text: Agreements with OpenAI and Meta drove the 82% rise in other revenue. Reservations and Waitlist are integrated into ChatGPT.

tailwinds.title: AI products
tailwinds.text: Yelp Host (2.5m annual run-rate calls, up 15x) and Smart Lead Reply (launching Q4 2026).

headwinds.title: Click erosion
headwinds.text: Ad clicks fell 8% in Q3 2026, after a 5% fall in Q2.

headwinds.title: SMB weakness
headwinds.text: Services advertising declined for the first time in at least nine quarters.

industry.source: Yelp Q3 2026 letter; PPC Land (Nov 2026); BriefGlance (Nov 2026); MarketBeat call summary (8 Nov 2026)

competition.title: The cheapest name among online local and vertical marketplaces
competition.subtitle: Higher returns on equity than most peers, at a fraction of the multiple
points: ROE rose to about 20% in 2025 as margins expanded and the share count fell.
Google is the dominant competitor for local intent; Angi and Thumbtack compete in home services.
porter: Google Maps/Search, Angi, Thumbtack, TripAdvisor, food-delivery apps for restaurants.
AI assistants that answer 'best plumber near me' directly.
The barrier is 20 years of reviews and a trusted brand. That data is hard to rebuild.
Traffic from Google and Apple; data partners (OpenAI, Meta) are also customers.
Hundreds of thousands of small advertisers, each with little power, but quick to cut budgets.
competition.source: Yelp filings; peer data from Yahoo Finance

theses.title: 1. The valuation assumes a decline worse than our bear case
theses.subtitle: Yelp generates ~$260m of free cash flow on an EV of ~$810m
points: EV/EBITDA is about 3.3x and P/E about 9x, against peer medians of about 9x and 17x.
Our structural-decline case assumes revenue falls 4% a year for five years and margins compress to 8%. It still gives $25 a share.
Net cash and ~$100m of quarterly operating cash flow give the company room to fund the pivot.
theses.risk: Revenue falls much faster than 4% a year as AI answers take over local discovery.
theses.source: Yahoo Finance via research pack; analyst scenarios

theses.title: 2. 'Other revenue' is a real second engine
theses.subtitle: Up 82% to a $136m run rate, targeting $250m by end-2028
points: Hatch's run-rate revenue reached ~$37m, up 55% year on year, with integrations into ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, Jobber and Workiz.
Data licensing with OpenAI and Meta turns AI from only a threat into a customer.
If other revenue reaches $250m, it would offset most of a mid-single-digit advertising decline.
theses.risk: Data-licensing deals are not renewed, or prices fall as AI companies find alternative data.

theses.title: 3. Capital return will restart in 2027
theses.subtitle: ~$200m bought back in 2026 to date; $339m of authorisation left
points: Yelp repurchased about $200m of stock in 2026 to date, about 18% of today's market value.
Buybacks are paused only to repay the $75m revolver drawn for Hatch, and are expected to resume in 2027.
At about 3x EBITDA, buybacks are among the best uses of cash available to management.
theses.risk: Further large acquisitions divert cash from buybacks.

comps.title: Yelp trades at a deep discount to local and vertical marketplaces
comps.subtitle: About 3x EBITDA vs a peer median of about 9x
comps.note: Peers: local, travel and vertical marketplaces selling advertising or leads to small businesses.

dcf.subtitle: Stabilisation case: revenue flat in 2026–27, then low growth; EBIT margin 11.5%; terminal growth cut to 1%

valuation.title: Most methods point well above the share price; analyst targets do not
points: Our $33 target is well above the $22 analyst median. We think consensus capitalises the advertising decline but not the cash flow and the new revenue lines.
The structural-decline scenario is the floor we watch: $25.

risks.title: AI search is the central risk; the balance sheet buys time

items.risk: AI answers keep cutting clicks and ad revenue
items.mitigant: Data licensing, Yelp Assistant and ChatGPT integrations turn AI into a distribution channel.
Cost discipline (product development costs –17% in Q3) keeps margins near 25% adjusted EBITDA.

items.risk: Hatch integration and the M&A strategy
items.mitigant: Hatch grew 55% after the deal. The revolver is being repaid before buybacks restart.

catalysts.what: Smart Lead Reply launch; ~$30m tax benefit.
Buybacks resume once the revolver is repaid.

risks.source: Yelp Q3 2026 letter and call; Yahoo Finance earnings calendar
